question: Can L2 regularization be used as a tunable external field that stabilizes successive rank-restricted features of a deep linear network, and can the resulting phase cascade be characterized exactly from both the macrostate singular values and the microscopic Hessian?

key_findings.claim: Under a simultaneous-alignment condition on the input and input-output covariances, the regularized deep-linear problem separates into one scalar potential per singular direction, so each newly learned direction raises the rank of every balanced layer and of the end-to-end map.
key_findings.evidence: At long times weight decay drives adjacent Gram-matrix differences to zero as exp(-2 beta t), giving 0-balanced factors with shared nonzero singular values. If Sigma_xx and Sigma_yx share the required singular frame, the loss reduces to L(sigma)=sum_j[kappa_j sigma_j^(2n)-2 eta_j sigma_j^n+n beta sigma_j^2]+tr(Sigma_yy); finite minima therefore index learned covariance directions and rank-restricted phases.

key_findings.claim: A network with one hidden layer undergoes a cascade of continuous second-order transitions at beta_j*=eta_j, in descending order of the singular values of Sigma_yx.
key_findings.evidence: For n=2 the per-direction potential is quartic, L_j=kappa_j sigma_j^4-2(eta_j-beta)sigma_j^2. Its minimum leaves zero continuously when beta drops below eta_j, with sigma_j proportional to sqrt(beta_j*-beta), critical exponent 1/2, and optimal factor singular value squared max((eta_j-beta)/kappa_j,0). The three-direction example eta=(0.95,0.55,0.30) reproduces the predicted rank ladder under numerical annealing.

key_findings.claim: With more than one hidden layer the same directions appear through discontinuous first-order transitions, with a metastable zero solution, a finite-amplitude local minimum, and separate bifurcation and equal-loss thresholds.
key_findings.evidence: For n>2 the potential contains a quadratic regularizer against higher-order data terms. Sigma_j=0 remains a local minimum; a nonzero local minimum first appears below beta_j,n^(det), then becomes globally preferred at the analytically derived level-crossing beta_j,n*. Deterministic gradient flow can remain trapped behind the barrier, whereas noise can produce rare escapes and hysteresis; reversed-annealing numerics for n=3 track the bifurcation and crossing curves.

key_findings.claim: The regularizer converts a distinguished subset of unregularized saddles into stable local minima: specifically, the solutions that are optimal under a rank constraint and retain the largest covariance directions.
key_findings.evidence: In the unregularized landscape, projections of Sigma_yx Sigma_xx^-1 onto ordered leading eigenspaces are higher-order saddles for ranks below full rank. At finite beta those same ordered rank-r solutions are local minima; as beta tends to zero they converge back to rank-restricted optima, while unordered selections remain strict saddles because an exchange mode can replace a weaker learned direction with a stronger one.

key_findings.claim: The microscopic Hessian admits a physically interpretable decomposition that matches the macrostate geometry rather than merely detecting scalar loss crossings.
key_findings.evidence: At a rank-r critical point the spectrum separates into data-dependent massive modes that change the product matrix, 4 beta modes from GL symmetries explicitly broken down to orthogonal symmetries, exact zero modes from surviving rotations, and null-sector modes. The number of data-dependent modes equals the dimension r(d_in+d_out-r) of the rank-r matrix manifold; the rank-r degeneracy has Stiefel-manifold dimension r(d_hidden-r)+r(r-1)/2 per hidden interface.

key_findings.claim: The continuous transition has both static and dynamical critical scaling.
key_findings.evidence: At a one-hidden-layer threshold the soft Hessian eigenvalue reaches zero, and an exactly solvable balanced gradient-flow case gives the critical singular value sigma_c(t)=sigma(0)/sqrt(1+4t sigma(0)^2), hence algebraic t^-1/2 decay instead of exponential relaxation. This connects the order-parameter exponent to critical slowing down.

key_findings.claim: The aligned infinite-data theory is qualitatively robust but not exact beyond its assumptions.
key_findings.evidence: For non-aligned covariances, numerical stationary solutions and perturbation theory show beta-dependent rotations of the singular vectors while preserving onset near the leading singular value. Finite-sample empirical covariances smear transition locations, and two-hidden-layer tanh networks on Gaussian data plus reused sigmoid-MNIST annealing results show discontinuous singular-value or effective-rank changes only qualitatively resembling the linear prediction.

method.core_idea: Treat the coefficient beta of layerwise Frobenius weight decay as an external field and follow equilibrium critical points as beta changes; use singular values of the end-to-end map as order parameters and the full parameter Hessian as the microscopic description.
method.mechanism: The derivation first uses regularization-induced 0-balancing to collapse a product of n factor matrices to shared singular values. Under aligned data covariances, the regularized MSE becomes a sum of independent Landau-like polynomial potentials. Their minima, bifurcations, and level crossings give rank transitions. The authors then lift each macro solution back to its degenerate factor-space orbit, diagonalize the Hessian into symmetry, null, exchange, and data sectors, compare its massive modes with the Jacobian of closed macro dynamics, and test perturbations with annealing simulations, finite-sample Gaussian data, and small nonlinear networks.
assumptions: The main exact results use deep linear feed-forward networks, squared error, layerwise L2 regularization, no architectural bottleneck, and gradient-flow equilibrium.
Inputs and outputs are zero-mean; Sigma_xx is invertible, Sigma_yx is full rank, and the population-data limit is used unless a finite-sample test is explicitly stated.
The closed scalar theory requires Sigma_xx and Sigma_yx to be simultaneously compatible with one singular-vector frame; generic non-aligned covariances couple singular values and vectors.
The clean cascade assumes distinct, ordered singular values; degeneracies can make several directions turn on together and enlarge the symmetry manifold.

Static phase claims are at zero temperature/noise and presume equilibration; finite learning rate, minibatch noise, and annealing direction affect escape from metastable minima in the first-order case.

techniques.role: Scans weight-decay strength to stabilize otherwise transient rank-restricted landscape levels.
Uses exponential Gram balancing to express all factors through shared nonzero singular values.
Reduces aligned population loss to independent polynomial potentials, one for each data singular direction.
Distinguishes creation of a metastable minimum from the beta value where it becomes the global phase.
Relates factor-space Hessian eigendirections to changes of the rank-constrained end-to-end matrix.
Counts zero and 4 beta modes created by surviving orthogonal and explicitly broken general-linear transformations.
Tracks stationary branches across beta, including metastable branches inaccessible from zero initialization.
Tests how singular values and vectors deform when exact simultaneous alignment is broken.

evaluations.setting: Aligned 3 x 3 Gaussian regression with eta=(0.95,0.55,0.30), equal hidden width, one or two hidden layers
evaluations.metric: Stationary singular values, loss/MSE branches, transition beta, and full Hessian spectrum
evaluations.result: Numerical forward and reverse annealing follow the analytic second-order rank onsets for one hidden layer and the bifurcation/level-crossing branches for two hidden layers; predicted Hessian sectors match numerical eigenvalues
evaluations.baseline: Closed-form scalar potentials and Hessian formulas

evaluations.setting: One-hidden-layer balanced gradient flow at the critical beta
evaluations.metric: Long-time decay of the critical singular mode
evaluations.result: The exact solution decays as t^-1/2
evaluations.baseline: Exponential relaxation away from a Hessian zero crossing

evaluations.setting: Non-aligned 2 x 2 covariance perturbation and finite empirical covariance samples
evaluations.metric: Macro singular values, right-singular-vector rotation, and onset location
evaluations.result: The leading onset persists while vectors rotate with beta and finite samples smear the transition

evaluations.setting: Two-hidden-layer tanh network on Gaussian data, hidden width 20, 20 trajectories
evaluations.metric: MSE and layer singular values over beta
evaluations.result: Discontinuous onsets remain qualitatively close to the deep-linear branches

evaluations.setting: Two-hidden-layer sigmoid network on MNIST, hidden width 128, annealing results imported from the authors' prior study
evaluations.metric: Accuracy, layer singular values, and effective rank
evaluations.result: Distinct accuracy changes coincide with rank-like jumps at moderate-to-large regularization, but the layers diverge from the linear picture for beta below roughly 0.02

limitations: Author-stated: exact transition points and separable order-parameter potentials require the covariance-alignment condition; generic covariances have beta-dependent singular vectors and no independent-mode reduction.
Author-stated: the central statistical-mechanics analysis is zero-temperature/zero-noise; whether finite-noise, large-width networks exhibit thermodynamic phase transitions remains open.
Author-stated: nonlinear-network evidence is numerical and only supports the linear description to some extent, with clear deviations at weak regularization.
Author-stated: finite datasets violate population covariance alignment and smear the predicted critical strengths.

Reviewer-identified: the first- versus second-order classification itself was already established by Ziyin and Ueda; the present novelty is the multidirectional cascade and geometry, not the existence of those two orders.

Reviewer-identified: deterministic first-order outcomes are initialization- and annealing-path-dependent because the zero and finite-rank minima coexist; an equilibrium level crossing does not predict which basin a practical optimizer reaches.

Reviewer-identified: calling the finite-dimensional zero-noise nonanalyticities phase transitions is a useful analogy, but it should not be conflated with a demonstrated thermodynamic-limit transition.
Reviewer-identified: the product-of-spheres description supplies the correct Stiefel-manifold dimension but is not generally a global topological factorization into independent spheres.

Reviewer-identified: the demonstrated features are singular directions of second-order Gaussian statistics; semantic features, classification boundaries, cross-entropy, normalization, residual paths, and realistic optimizers are not covered.
Reviewer-identified: the MNIST evidence is reused from prior work and is not an independent large-scale validation of the new Hessian theory.
failure_modes: Repeated or nearly repeated covariance singular values can merge nominally separate transitions and make the ordered feature identity unstable.
A singular Sigma_xx, rank-deficient Sigma_yx, or a hidden bottleneck violates the main setup and changes the admissible rank ladder.
Non-aligned covariances couple order parameters, so applying beta_j*=eta_j direction by direction can give wrong transition locations and vectors.
For n>2, zero or small initialization can remain trapped in the trivial metastable basin even below the equal-loss threshold; reverse annealing can trace a branch that forward training never reaches.
Minibatch or injected noise can induce barrier crossings and hysteresis, invalidating a purely stationary deterministic prediction of the trained rank.
At weak regularization a nonlinear model can leave the linear-origin regime, after which layer ranks and singular onsets need not remain synchronized.
A finite-data covariance realization can reorder weak modes, smear thresholds, and make a purported feature cascade sample-specific.
Regularization can stabilize a rank-restricted solution that is useful as a geometric probe but suboptimal for predictive accuracy, so detected phases are not automatically desirable models.
reusable_insights: Scan a controllable regularizer and monitor order parameters plus curvature to expose intermediate representations that ordinary training visits only transiently.
Separate a branch's birth point, equal-objective crossing, and dynamical escape point; they answer different questions in a metastable landscape.
Use end-to-end singular values for functional rank while retaining factor-space Hessian sectors to distinguish real feature changes from symmetry motion.
Rank-restricted optima provide a bridge between early-stopped saddle-to-saddle learning and regularizer-stabilized stationary models.
Before extrapolating a mode-wise theory, test covariance commutation, spectral gaps, and finite-sample stability; these determine whether feature labels remain meaningful.
A zero Hessian block can encode benign parameter redundancy, whereas data-dependent soft modes forecast an actual functional transition.
open_questions: Can the cascade be characterized for generic noncommuting covariances without reducing the solution to independent singular modes?
What are the finite-width and finite-temperature scaling laws for transition rounding, metastable lifetimes, and hysteresis under minibatch SGD?
Which order parameters replace end-to-end singular values in nonlinear, normalized, residual, attention, or convolutional architectures?
Can a beta-annealing feature detector recover semantically stable features on real datasets rather than only covariance directions?
How do repeated spectra, architectural bottlenecks, classification loss, and label noise alter the number and order of transitions?
Can Hessian softening be used prospectively to choose an annealing schedule without solving or diagonalizing the full landscape?

competitive_landscape.title: Exact Phase Transitions in Deep Learning
competitive_landscape.difference: Ziyin and Ueda already prove that L2-regularized one-hidden-layer linear nets have a second-order onset and deeper nets a first-order onset; the later journal version also gives a linear-origin theorem for nonlinear nets. The present paper extends that scalar/onset picture to arbitrary input-output dimension, resolves a cascade indexed by individual covariance modes, and derives the associated full Hessian and macro geometry.

competitive_landscape.title: Phase transitions reveal hierarchical structure in deep neural networks
competitive_landscape.difference: Ersoy et al. phenomenologically use L2 scans to expose accuracy basins, saddle structure, and mode connectivity in nonlinear MNIST networks. The present work supplies an exactly tractable deep-linear model for those observations; its nonlinear results remain qualitative and partly reuse that study.

competitive_landscape.title: Implicit Bias of SGD in L2-Regularized Linear DNNs: One-Way Jumps from High to Low Rank
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang and Jacot study stochastic escape among rank-indexed local minima in weakly regularized deep linear matrix completion and prove one-way high-to-low-rank accessibility. This paper instead maps equilibrium branches while beta itself changes, includes second-order and first-order cascades, and gives exact Hessian sectors under aligned Gaussian regression, but does not prove noisy escape rates.

competitive_landscape.title: Saddle-to-Saddle Dynamics in Deep Linear Networks: Small Initialization Training, Symmetry, and Sparsity
competitive_landscape.difference: Jacot et al. analyze unregularized small-initialization dynamics that visit increasing-rank saddles over time. The present paper offers a static analogue: finite weight decay turns selected rank-restricted saddles into minima that can be examined at equilibrium and traversed by changing beta.

competitive_landscape.title: Regularization Implies balancedness in the deep linear network
competitive_landscape.difference: Lindsey and Menon use geometric invariant theory to show L2 regularization minimizes along symmetry fibers at the balanced manifold and separates regularizing from learning flows. The current paper uses the resulting 0-balanced reduction as machinery for mode-wise phase thresholds, rank-restricted minima, and a Hessian phase taxonomy.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: this is the first in-depth, largely analytic treatment of a regularizer-induced cascade of static phase transitions in deep linear networks of arbitrary depth and input-output dimension, connecting learnable features, order parameters, exact transition points, full Hessian spectra, and macro dynamics. Prior work already established the one-hidden-layer second-order versus deeper first-order distinction, exact regularized deep-linear minima, regularization-induced balancing, stochastic jumps among rank minima, and unregularized saddle-to-saddle rank growth. Reviewer inference: the defensible novelty is therefore not 'weight decay causes phase transitions,' but the mode-resolved cascade under aligned covariances, its exact rank-by-rank thresholds and metastable branches, and the detailed micro-to-macro Hessian accounting that turns earlier phenomenology into a coherent solvable model. Generalization from covariance modes to semantic features or genuine finite-temperature phase behavior is suggestive rather than demonstrated.
reviewer_notes: The full 39-page extraction was read, including the critical-point, Hessian, macro-Jacobian, numerical, and exact-dynamics appendices. Formula and transition anchors refer to local PDF pages. Competing mechanisms were checked against primary arXiv/OpenReview records. Author claims and reviewer inferences are labeled separately, especially where the paper uses statistical-physics terminology or imports nonlinear evidence from prior work.
